title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of direction indicators for power-driven vehicles and their trailers (version 2.0.0)
scope_summary: UN R6 approves types of direction indicator lamps, which are fixed-position flashing light devices of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 5 and 6, including their light sources, light source modules and variable intensity controls. It applies to direction indicators intended for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O and T, while installation on the vehicle is governed by UN Regulation No. 48.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to direction indicators for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O, and T. [...] The present Regulation applies solely to fixed-position flashing light devices whose flashing is obtained by the intermittent supply of electric current to the lamp.
applies_to_components: Rear direction indicators of categories 2a (steady luminous intensity) and 2b (variable luminous intensity)
Side direction indicators of categories 5 and 6
Direction indicators forming an assembly of two lamps (marking 'D')
Direction indicators with sequential activation of light sources
Non-replaceable filament lamps / non-replaceable light sources
Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that include a direction indicator function
Lamps reciprocally incorporated with headlamps that share a lens
relation_to_other_regulations: UN R48: its definitions apply to this Regulation (para. 1.2); installation of direction indicators on vehicles is governed by R48
UN R37: filament lamp categories and standard (étalon) filament lamps prescribed for replaceable light sources must come from R37
UN R128: LED light source categories and standard (étalon) LED light sources must come from R128
Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that comply with several UN Regulations may carry a single international approval mark (para. 4.1.2, 4.3)
Lamps may share a lens with headlamps approved under other headlamp regulations (para. 4.3.3)
Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 is referenced for the vehicle category definitions and for the distinguishing numbers of Contracting Parties
Approval numbers currently start with 01 (01 series of amendments); the 02 series of amendments does not require a change in the approval number

defined_terms.definition: A device mounted on a motor vehicle or trailer which, when operated by the driver, signals the driver's intention to change the vehicle's direction, limited to fixed-position flashing light devices whose flashing is obtained by intermittent electric supply.

Lamps differing in essential respects such as trade name or mark, optical system characteristics (intensity, light distribution, light source category, light source module), category, variable intensity control or sequential activation; a change of light source or filter colour does not constitute a change of type.

defined_terms.label: 2.1, Annex 1
defined_terms.definition: Front direction indicator categories, distinguished according to Annex 1 by distance to the dipped-beam headlamp and the associated intensity requirements.
Rear direction indicator with steady luminous intensity.
Rear direction indicator with variable luminous intensity, provided by a variable intensity control delivering two intensity levels.

defined_terms.label: 2.1, Annex 1
defined_terms.definition: Side direction indicator categories, which differ in their geometric visibility and light-distribution angles according to Annex 1.

defined_terms.label: 1.3(d), 2.2.3
defined_terms.definition: A system that ensures the two levels of luminous intensity of a category 2b direction indicator.

defined_terms.label: 1.3(e)
defined_terms.definition: The activation of the light sources of a direction indicator in sequence, which is a type-distinguishing feature unless the modes are selectable without any optical change.

defined_terms.label: 2.2.1(c), 4.2.2.3
defined_terms.definition: A combination of interdependent lamps that together fulfil the direction indicator function, marked 'Y' and submitted for approval by one applicant (definition per R48).
Two lamps of the same category that together perform the function, marked 'D'.
A light source unit specific to the lamp that carries its own trade name, an 'MD' identification code and rated voltage marking.
Electronic gear controlling the light source; if it is not in the lamp body it must bear the manufacturer's name and identification number.

defined_terms.term: Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps
defined_terms.definition: Multi-function lamp assemblies that may carry a single approval mark when each function complies with its respective UN Regulation.
A light distribution in conformity with para. 2.1.3 of Annex 4, indicated by a downward vertical arrow from a horizontal segment.

applicability_hints: Any multi-function front or rear lamp cluster (combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated) that contains a turn-signal function needs R6 approval for that function, shown by category symbols 1/1a/1b/2a/2b/5/6 within a shared approval mark.
Side repeaters, including those integrated in exterior mirror housings or fenders, fall under R6 as category 5 or 6 devices.
Light source modules used in direction indicators must carry their own 'MD' code and approval marking, so module suppliers are affected.

Electronic light source control gear or variable intensity controls located outside the lamp body are part of the lamp and must be marked with manufacturer name and ID number; ECUs providing the 2b intensity signal must be submitted with the application.
Sequential (dynamic/'running') turn indicators are covered, and sequential activation is a type-distinguishing feature.
Headlamps or lamps sharing a lens with a direction indicator are affected through para. 4.3.3.

Applies only to fixed-position electrically flashed lamps, so mechanical semaphore-arm indicators are not covered; flasher units themselves are not approved here, although activation information is required.
The hazard warning signal uses the same lamps, but its installation and operation are governed by R48, not R6.
Replaceable light sources prescribed in the lamp must be R37 filament lamps or R128 LED light sources, which links bulb and LED light source choice to R6 approval.
Lamps for trailers (O), tractors (T) and L-category vehicles are within the stated scope.
